title: POST /control/{action} and /plan/apply take unvalidated dicts: a non-numeric hours or soc_pct answers 500 instead of a 422 refusal
label: bug
steps: As an operator: POST /api/sites/<id>/control/hold with body {"hours": "four"} (or {"soc_pct": "abc"}, or {"hours": {}}). `float(inp.get("hours", 4) or 4)` on line 154 and `float(inp.get("soc_pct") ...)` on line 161 raise ValueError/TypeError, which no route-level handler catches; api.py's catch-all (line 317-321) turns it into 500 'The server could not answer this request'. Same shape on POST /plan/apply (line 94: raw dict, `str(inp.get("day"))[:10]` accepts any junk as the day_local key that control_state later matches against today).
expected: HANDOFF §4 'Strict models: request models forbid unknown fields. A refusal is a Refusal(status, sentence, code)'; plan Part 2.8 untrusted input; the page expects a one-sentence 422 it can show in the dialog (control-actions.tsx line 100).
actual: A malformed body is a 500 server fault with a request id, logged as a crash; unknown fields are silently accepted; `day` is stored unvalidated (e.g. 'yesterday' or '2026-13-45').
evidence: routes_plans.py:152-168 (`inp: dict = Body(default={})`, float() calls); routes_plans.py:94-103; api.py:317-321 generic except -> 500. Contrast sites.OverrideFields (sites.py:366-370) which is a Strict model, and routes_sites.overrides_post which uses it.

title: Advisory tier: the 'table to key in' is re-compiled every 15 minutes, so the installer's keyed table is a moving target and no daily table / write budget exists as Part 7.1 step 7 requires

area: Control: vendor table / Mark as applied
steps: At an advisory_writes site (e.g. the demo textile plant), open /sites/:id/control, copy the table, mark it applied for today. Wait for the next tick (15 min; or press Re-solve now). Reload Control: `comp = plans.current(site_id)['slots']` now shows the new plan's table (different boundaries after a forecast update), the header still reads 'Following plan (table applied)' (control_state keys on any applied row for today), and nothing on the page says which table the installer actually keyed or that today's keyed table differs from the one shown.
expected: Plan Part 7.1 step 7: 'the nightly table write after the 23:00 solve; an event rewrite only when the expected rupee gain exceeds a threshold (default Rs 500), the budget allows and the previous write is more than 60 minutes old'; Part 7.6: the installer keys the day's table and the product confirms that table from telemetry; UI-15 'the capabilities card with budgets used today'. The installer needs one stable daily table (plus an explicit 'a better table is worth Rs X, re-key?' nudge).
actual: delivery.compile_mode_a is run on every tick and the control page always shows the current plan's table; `budget.used_today` counts plan_messages rows, which are written only on an edge key pull (routes_edge.py:410-427), so at a keyed-table site it is always '0 of 3' and never enforced; the applied log links a plan_id but the page never shows that plan's table against the current one. The tracker marks DLV-01 (write budget, 60-minute spacing) as [~].
evidence: routes_plans.py:133-148 (control: `comp = (p or {}).get('slots')`, `writes_today` from plan_messages); routes_sites.py:47-52 (control_state 'following' on any applied row today); vendor-table.tsx:52-68 (days from control.compiled, table of the current plan); plans.py:391-470 (every tick compiles and stores slots; no budget logic); EMS_BUILD_PROGRESS.md:185 DLV-01 [~].

title: After a CSV upload the chart, data-quality strip and imports log do not refresh (wrong query keys invalidated)
label: bug
steps: On /sites/:id/telemetry choose a custom range covering the file's days, upload a CSV. The green result notice appears, but the chart above keeps 'No data in this range', the Data quality card still says 'No CSV has been uploaded' and the Imports table is empty until the 5-minute poll or a reload.
expected: The page's own data (qk.telemetry, qk.qualityAll, qk.heatmap) re-read after an import, as the control page does after an action.
actual: onSuccess invalidates only `qk.site(siteId)`; keys.ts says qk.site(id) is a prefix of the site's queries, but qk.site(id) = ['gl','site',id] is only a prefix if invalidateQueries is called with that exact array — check: qk.telemetry = ['gl','site',id,'telemetry',q], which IS under the prefix, yet `useQuery` for telemetry has `enabled: !problem` and placeholderData, so a custom-range query refetches; the quality query (refetchInterval 5 min) is also under the prefix. If the prefix invalidation does reach them this finding reduces to: the Devices page's 14-day quality and the heatmap (staleTime 15 min) refetch, but the chart's dataset for a *preset* range ending now never includes historical rows anyway. Reported at low severity and 0.5 confidence because it depends on React Query prefix matching of qk.site.
evidence: csv-upload.tsx:48-51; keys.ts:32-43; telemetry-page.tsx:62-74.

title: SoC chart has no temperature axis and no outage hatching; the SoC tile says 'estimated' even when the value is the BMS reading
label: ux
area: Battery page SoC chart and KPI
steps: battery_page returns battery_temp_c in `soc.series` (routes_telemetry.py 286) but SocChart plots only SoC est/BMS, plan SoC, reserve and power; TimeSeriesChart supports `bands` yet none are passed for outages. For a BMS-only source, battery.state uses `est = where(isnan(soc), soc_bms, soc)` (battery.py 23) so soc_pct equals the BMS value; the tile is still titled 'State of charge (estimated)' with sub 'BMS 37.2 %' repeating the same number, and the server does not say which column it used.
expected: R8 2.10: 'SoC chart ... temperature on the second axis, outages hatched'; design rule 2.21: 'Estimated marks ... SoC from an estimate rather than a BMS', and for OEM-cloud sources 'the trust card explains the estimate is cloud-side'.
actual: Temperature fetched and dropped (only the last reading appears in the pack card); no outage bands; 'estimated' label regardless of source.
evidence: battery-charts.tsx 253-262 series list; battery-kpis.tsx 100; battery.py 23, 42-44 (trust gap only where both measured, so a BMS-only site scores a high trust with no independent check).

Tracker line 161 marks UI-11 [x] as showing 'the fuel-curve fit against observed'. BACKEND_ASKS lists the refit.

label: spec-mismatch

expected: R8 2.10 'economics card (purchase price, warranted throughput, derived wear cost): owner and analyst only'; plan 9.4: operator sees 'costs but not money settings'; replacement cost and warranty are money settings (edit_money_settings, DESIGN_LOG rounds 1-2).

title: Forecast refresh is open to operators and bypasses the tick's observed-outage protection
label: spec-mismatch
steps: (a) auth.need('run_jobs') with run_jobs = {admin, operator, analyst} (auth.py 41); stage-card.tsx 39 says 'for an administrator, an operator or an analyst'. (b) The route calls forecast.issue(s, now_ts()) with save=True: save_forecast does INSERT OR REPLACE on (site, kind, belief_time = align(now)) (telemetry.py 602-608), replacing the issue the current plan was built on at the same quarter, and without plans._keep_observed_outage (plans.py 385-400), the rule DESIGN_LOG rounds 1-2 settled ('a same-quarter re-solve never replaces an issue that observed an outage with a blind one').
expected: R8 2.8 / plan 9.4: retrain or refresh is for owner and analyst; the plan's 10.5 permission table has no run_jobs. A manual refresh should either go through the same protection as the tick or not overwrite the tick's stored issue.
actual: Operators can refresh; a refresh while a batch is more than OBSERVED_LAG_MIN minutes in flight can store a blind issue over an observed one, which the scores and the forecasts page then show.
evidence: routes_forecasts.py 29-31; telemetry.save_forecast; plans.tick 398-400.

title: Accuracy summary: 'last 7 days' is the last 7 scored rows, PV has no persistence baseline so no skill, and only one horizon class exists
label: spec-mismatch
area: Forecasts page accuracy tiles and daily scores
steps: forecast.scores(): summary.last7 = mean(v[-7:]) over whatever days were scored in the window (a site with gaps gets older days); score_day writes a load baseline (same weekday last week, lines 458-463) and an outage schedule-only baseline, but no PV baseline, so the PV tiles show nRMSE with no skill; every row is horizon_class 'day_ahead'.
expected: Plan 5.5 pre-registered metrics: PV 'skill scored per horizon class' against smart persistence (the stage-1 gate is 25 % skill at 6-24 h); R8 2.8 accuracy card 'daytime PV nRMSE and skill vs smart persistence'; tracker line 133 claims 'accuracy to date by horizon class'.
actual: nRMSE and Brier only, day-ahead only; the tile label says 'last 7 days'.
evidence: forecast.py scores(): `vals7 = [x['value'] for x in v[-7:]]`; score_day(): baseline only `if kind == 'load'` and for outage; accuracy-cards.tsx 19.

title: Stage wording says stage 0 lasts 'until the site has a week of its own data' but PV and load reach stage 1 after 3 days; the critical-load line uses the 'unserved' colour
label: ux
